A.explanation: This is about $8.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, which is the fringe spacing $x$ itself, not the slit separation $a$ found from $a=\lambda D/x$.

B.explanation: This results from using $x = 34/5 \text{ mm}$, but the $34 \text{ mm}$ across five bright fringes contains only four fringe spacings.

C.explanation: With $x = 34/4 \text{ mm} = 8.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, $a = \lambda D/x$ gives about $1.9 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$.

D.explanation: This results from using $x = 34 \text{ mm}$ as one spacing, omitting the division by the four intervals between the five fringes.

hints: Notice the $34 \text{ mm}$ arrow starts on one bright fringe and ends four gaps later on the fifth bright fringe, so count the fringe spacings between them.
Recall the double-slit fringe formula $x = \lambda D/a$, where $x$ is one fringe spacing, $\lambda = 680 \text{ nm}$ and $D = 2.4 \text{ m}$.
First calculate $x$ in metres from $34 \text{ mm}$ divided by the number of spacings, then rearrange to $a = \lambda D/x$ and check the power of ten.
walkthrough: Convert the given quantities to SI units: $\lambda = 680 \text{ nm} = 680 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$, $D = 2.4 \text{ m}$, total measured length $= 34 \text{ mm} = 34 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$.
Find one fringe spacing $x$ from the diagram. Five bright fringes in a row are separated by four equal gaps, so $x = 34 \times 10^{-3}/4 = 8.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$.
State the double-slit interference relation for fringe spacing: $x = \lambda D/a$, so slit separation $a = \lambda D/x$.
Calculate: numerator $= 1.632 \times 10^{-6}$, then $a = 1.632 \times 10^{-6}/8.5 \times 10^{-3} \approx 1.92 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$, about $1.9 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$. This is option C.
